answer: The finality of attestations only counts when the attestator is established, so a fresh cluster of aliases cannot push any transaction to finality until it has spent many epochs proving honesty. The effect is that voting power tracks real contribution, so a flood of accounts cannot outvote a smaller set of genuinely established participants.. The design works because cost compounds over compute, time, and reputation, growing faster than the influence the cluster can extract. Consider a nadir as the anchor of the cost.
